title: Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union)
summary: Union-Find (DSU) manages a partition of elements into disjoint sets. Operations: find(x) returns the representative of x's set, union(x,y) merges the sets of x and y. Optimizations: path compression (flatten tree during find), union by rank/size (attach smaller tree to larger). Amortized O(α(n)) per operation (α = inverse Ackermann, effectively constant).

structure.meaning: parent[i] = parent of element i. Root has parent[i] = i (or -1).
rank[i] = height of tree rooted at i (or size of set). Used for union by rank/size.
Recursively find root. Path compression: set parent of each visited node to root.
Find roots of x and y. If different, attach shorter tree to taller tree. If equal rank, increment rank.
Attach smaller set to larger set. Update size of larger set.
α(n) ≤ 4 for all practical n (n ≤ 2^2^2^2^2^2^2...). Effectively constant.

notes: Union-Find is used in Kruskal's MST algorithm, connected components, and network connectivity.
Path compression + union by rank gives amortized O(α(n)) per operation.
Union-Find is not a tree (it's a forest with path compression).
Persistent Union-Find supports rollback (used in offline algorithms).
Weighted Union-Find tracks additional data (e.g., parity, distance).
